title: Run D-1
subtitle: MnGeSe doped with Ti: synthesis → optics + DFT → strained film
task: Dope MnGeSe with Ti past the critical content where its structure distorts, and deliver a single-phase distorted pellet whose magnetic ordering temperature is 186.2 ± 3 K, diagnosing what went wrong with the group's pilot pellet on the way. Then measure the pellet's optical gap and find the Hubbard U at which DFT+U reproduces it, with a converged k-point table. Finally predict and grow a strained film whose gap is 0.62 ± 0.04 eV, and blind-predict a second film. One budget of 62 lab actions covers all three stages; the agent works through a Linux desktop (GSAS-II, LibreOffice Calc, a text editor).

outcome.headline: All eleven checks passed: the right distorted pellet, a converged U from the optical gap, and a film inside the device window, with 61 of 62 actions used.

steps.obs:
{"brief":"Project: MnGeSe doped with Ti. One budget of 62 lab actions and one ledger for
the whole project. Read ~/lab/lab_manual.md first; rules, thresholds and conversions are there.
Free files: lab_manual.md, vegard_C2_Ti.csv, substrates.csv, the parent CIF (reference_cif).
Segments run in order. Close each one with lab__deliver(segment, item, answer). The answer is frozen
in the ledger. After A closes, only the pellet you delivered and films grown from it can be measured.
Safety: …
events: Pilot pellet P001: the furnace runs 55 C below its setpoint (reached 580 C of 635 C), leaving 14.0 wt% unreacted precursor

steps.say: Let me open the manual in the Text Editor.
Maximize and enable word wrap.
Word wrap is under Document.
Reading the lab files (manual, Vegard table, substrates) before planning synthesis.
Measured the Si reference and P001 XRD; now I'll inspect the patterns to get the instrument zero and P001's phases.
Locating the Si(111) peak in the reference to determine the diffractometer zero offset.
GSAS-II is open; importing the P001 powder pattern to check its phases.
Selecting the instrument parameter file for the import.

events: S001: furnace actually reached 715 C (setpoint 770 C)
S001: true x = 0.245 (nominal 0.25); distorted branch, single phase; true ordering temperature 180.1 K (target 186.2 K)

steps.say: S001 (x=0.25 nominal) orders at ≈179 K vs P001 ≈169 K, so Tc rises with x. Checking S001's actual composition from its XRD.
S001: c≈8.714 Å → x_actual≈0.244 (close to nominal). Interpolating Tc vs x suggests x≈0.30 for 186 K.
events: S002: furnace actually reached 730 C (setpoint 785 C)
S002: true x = 0.293 (nominal 0.3); distorted branch, single phase; true ordering temperature 194.7 K (target 186.2 K)

steps.say: S002 orders at ≈195 K — overshoots. Checking its composition.
S002: c≈8.694 Å → x≈0.293, Tc≈195 K. Interpolating between S001 (0.244, ~180 K) and S002 gives x_actual≈0.263 for 186 K → nominal 0.27.
events: S003: furnace actually reached 720 C (setpoint 775 C)
S003: true x = 0.264 (nominal 0.27); distorted branch, single phase; true ordering temperature 186.0 K (target 186.2 K)

steps.say: S003 (nominal 0.27) orders at ≈186 K — on target. Now examining its XRD in GSAS-II (phase purity and cell).
S003 shows no 27.85° impurity peak. Zooming in to check the distortion splitting.
S003 is single-phase with a split (102)/(012) doublet → orthorhombic (a≠b) distortion. Now refining the cell in GSAS-II.
Extension filter is case-sensitive; switching it.
Linking the phase to the S003 histogram only.
Setting the instrument zero (+0.01°, from the Si reference) on the S003 histogram, then refining.
Saving the GSAS-II project so the refinement can run.
Refinement converging (Rw≈11.9): a≈3.784, b≈3.748, c≈8.707 Å. Running one more cycle.
Converged: a=3.7843, b=3.7484, c=8.7065 Å → a_inplane=3.7664 Å; Vegard gives x≈0.266 (from a) and 0.263 (from c), so x_actual≈0.264.
Delivering segment A with S003.
events: Delivered S003: true x = 0.264, distorted, single phase, ordering temperature 186.0 K
S003: true optical gap 0.757 eV; true effective U 6.92 eV

steps.say: Measured S003 absorption; now doing the Tauc analysis in Calc.
Opening the absorption data in LibreOffice Calc for a Tauc fit.
Setting up Tauc columns in Calc (the range jump isn't registering; pressing Enter explicitly).
Making an XY scatter Tauc plot of (αE)² vs E.
The "\n" in typed text isn't committing cells here; I'll enter one formula at a time with an explicit Enter.
Tauc fit gives gap ≈ 0.760 eV (0.756–0.762 across fit windows, R²=0.996). Re-checking the manual's DFT rules before running calculations.
Manual noted: k* rule (0.01 eV gap, 1 meV/atom, need a denser mesh), ground state = lowest E per f.u. (FM 1 f.u., stripe 2, checker 4). Starting the k-convergence series at x=0.264.
events: k-mesh n = 4 is not converged: total energy off by 100.51 meV/atom (gap unaffected)
k-mesh n = 6 is not converged: total energy off by 43.51 meV/atom (gap unaffected)
k-mesh n = 8 is not converged: total energy off by 23.56 meV/atom (gap unaffected)
k-mesh n = 10 is not converged: total energy off by 14.32 meV/atom (gap unaffected)
k-mesh n = 12 is not converged: total energy off by 9.31 meV/atom (gap unaffected)

steps.say: FM at U=3 prints only a Fermi level (no gap, i.e. metallic). Checking the other k-meshes.
k-series so far (FM, U=3, Ry): k4 −211.02784, k6 −211.04041, k8 −211.04481, k10 −211.04684, k12 −211.04795 — k10→12 still 5 meV/atom, so I need denser meshes.
events: k-mesh n = 16 is not converged: total energy off by 4.32 meV/atom (gap unaffected)

steps.say: k16: −211.04905 Ry. The k-series follows E ≈ E∞ + 0.362/n² Ry, so k* will be around 24 (needs a 28 in the table). First I'll map spin configs and U cheaply at k=12.
events: k-mesh n = 12 is not converged: total energy off by 9.31 meV/atom (gap unaffected)
k-mesh n = 12 is not converged: total energy off by 9.31 meV/atom (gap unaffected)

steps.say: U=3, k12 per f.u.: FM −211.04795, stripe −211.04362, checker −211.05014 Ry → AFM-checker lowest (≈30 meV/f.u. below FM), but all metallic. Scanning U upward for checker.
events: k-mesh n = 12 is not converged: gap off by +0.345 eV, energy off by 9.31 meV/atom

steps.say: U=5 checker: gap 0.594 eV. Need larger U; trying U=6.
events: k-mesh n = 12 is not converged: gap off by +0.345 eV, energy off by 9.31 meV/atom
k-mesh n = 8 is not converged: gap off by +0.893 eV, energy off by 23.56 meV/atom
k-mesh n = 12 is not converged: gap off by +0.345 eV, energy off by 9.31 meV/atom

steps.say: k26: gap 0.419 eV, so the gap converges as g∞ + B/n² with B≈63 eV (k8/k12/k26 all fit). k12 overestimates by ~0.44 eV, so U must be retuned at production k. Checking k32.
k32 gap equals k26 (0.4186 eV) and energies agree to 0.33 meV/atom → k*=26. The gap at converged k is 0.419 eV at U=5.6, so U must rise; trying U=6.8 at k26.
U=6.8 → gap 0.728 eV; with U=5.6 → 0.419 eV, linear interpolation gives U≈6.92 for 0.760 eV. Checking ground state (FM, stripe) at U=6.92, k26.
Now Segment C. Checking substrates.csv.
Misfits vs a_inplane 3.7664 Å: YSZ −3.8%, YAlO3 −1.5%, NdGaO3 +2.4%, LSAT +2.7%, SrTiO3 +3.7%, NdScO3 +6.3%. Probing the gap vs. strain with checker at U=6.92, ε=+0.02.
Tensile strain raises the gap (0.941 eV at +2%), so the device needs compression. Linear estimate: ε≈−1.5%, which matches YAlO3. Computing all three spin configs at ε=−0.015.
Checker at ε=−1.5% gives 0.620 eV, on target. Checking the FM and stripe energies.
At ε=−1.5%, per f.u.: checker −212.42929 < stripe −212.42548 < FM −212.42193 Ry, so checker stays the ground state and ΔE ≈ −100.2 meV/f.u. Checking the budget before I commit.
17 actions left: 8 for the two films, and 4 more for the U±0.3 ΔE interval. Committing the strain prediction now, before any growth.
I need K_relax from the manual to pick a coherent thickness.

events: Film F001 on YAlO3, 25 nm: lattice mismatch -1.49%, true strain -1.23% (partly relaxed); true gap 0.643 eV (device window 0.62 ± 0.04 eV)

steps.say: Analysing the F001 film scan: the 00l lines against the YAlO3 (001) reference line at d=3.71 Å.
Each line is 0.02°: line = (2θ−10)/0.02 + 2. Jumping to the substrate line near 23.97° (line ≈700).
Substrate Kα1 centroid ≈23.974° vs 23.966° calculated, so zero ≈ +0.008°. Now the film (004) near 41°.
(004) is weak: Kα1 ≈41.11°. Cross-checking with the (003) line near 30.5° for precision.
